text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: vpc-egress-error-rate spike in eu-west-3 (service: inference-hosting) — 4xx/5xx increase, key customers reporting failures. Paging Sam (oncall).

Sam: got the page, looking. seeing traffic error spike on egress from az-c pods to internet NAT. symptoms: TCP RSTs, some services time out. pulling logs.

Priya: I'm on networking. any chance of recent route changes or TGW updates? I see a terraform apply ~20m ago touching route-table association for az-c-private-subnets.

Sam: yep saw a deploy around that time. alerting infra and checking metrics: CloudWatch NAT Gateway HealthyHostCount shows partial healthy in az-c, but az-a/b ok. Both new and existing connections affected; seems sticky for some source IPs.

Miguel: joining. can you paste the failing logs or flows? netflow shows asymmetric returns from NAT in az-c -> responses returning via az-a NAT (wrong AZ). Connection tracking mismatch.

Sam: paste of flow sample:
```
SRC: 10.10.72.54:34012 -> 44.55.66.77:443 SYN
Forwarded to nat-azc -> then SYN-ACK back from 44.55.66.77 -> nat-aza and gets DNAT to different EIP
Result: conntrack sees different path -> RSTs
```

Priya: that sounds like route table assoc drift. az-c private subnets might be associated to the wrong route table that has no NAT-GW route or has target to a TGW attachment. checking:
`aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=rt-priv-azc` -> shows route to 0.0.0.0/0 target: tgw-0abcd (unexpected)

Chun: who ran the terraform? I see PR #1247 merged by infra-bot 18m ago which included a change to `modules/network/route_tables.tf` with a conditional for TGW attach. looks like the module allowed TGW bind for az-c incorrectly.

Sam: immediate mitigation: can we re-associate the private subnets in az-c back to their previous route table that has NAT target? Priya, can you run re-assoc now? I want to avoid zombies.

Priya: running re-assoc now. command:
```
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-0ff12345 --subnet-id subnet-0c12345a
```
Trying for three subnets.

OpsBot: system note: route-table association changed by Priya at 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z (api)

Priya: associations done. verifying connectivity and conntrack warmup.

Miguel: running quick curl tests against affected endpoints from az-c host: success now for new requests, but long-lived connections need reconnection. starting canary ramp to customers.

Sam: alerting Customer Success: some customers experienced short-lived failures for API calls in eu-west-3. no data loss, retries should succeed. tagging support tickets.

SRE-Oncall-2: observing metrics — error rates falling, latency normalizing. NAT gateway healthy hosts back to expected levels after assoc.

Chun: reverting the terraform change is necessary. PR change introduced conditional variable `enable_tgw_by_az` and defaulted true for az-c. that should have been false. filing rollback PR and will coordinate safe reapply with lock.

Miguel: action item: add guardrail to the module to prevent TGW attach when `env=prod` unless an explicit opt-in in the account. Also add a unit test for plan diffs that assert no route table swap unless approval label present.

Priya: tagging the change as hotfix: PR #1250 created to revert the change in `modules/network/route_tables.tf` and to add a `prevent_unexpected_tgw_attach` flag. will request urgent review from infra team.

Sam: handoff: I need to go to meetings in ~20m. SRE-Oncall-2 will take active watch. leave runbook notes below.

Sam: RUNBOOK (quick):
- if API error spike in eu-west-3 and netflow shows asymmetric returns -> check route-table associations for private subnets in affected AZ.
- `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=<subnet>` to confirm route table.
- ensure 0.0.0.0/0 route points to nat-gw-<az> EIP: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids rtb-...` and inspect Routes[].Target.
- temporary mitigation: `associate-route-table` to restore to nat-enabled RT.
- long-term: revert terraform PR and add module guardrails.

OpsBot: PagerDuty note: incident escalated to SEV-2 at 2026-03-15T14:05:12Z, de-escalated to monitoring at 2026-03-15T14:24:30Z.

Priya: posting post-incident next steps in #eng-networking, will attach diff and the repro commands.

Chun: creating a follow-up ticket: INFRA-987 - "Prevent accidental TGW attach to prod private RTs" assigning to network team, due in 3 days.

SRE-Oncall-2: continuing 1h watch and will perform health-check sweep every 10m. leaving handoff note to next oncall.

Sam: thanks everyone. summary for CS: brief outage window ~14:05-14:20 UTC, affected subset of eu-west-3 customers with in-flight requests; most requests retried and succeeded. No data integrity impact. follow-up: roll back PR, module tests, and postmortem.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated, monitoring. Root cause: incorrect terraform change that associated az-c private subnets to TGW route table (no NAT egress), causing asymmetric return traffic and conntrack failures.
